## Maintainer ruling — decision batch #49, item 4: **B — act on the organization's claim, never on the user**

Recorded by the director seat (session `session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um`) from the maintainer's live reply to batch #49, verbatim: 「**15041 应该改为实际 id 保存。选A，其他同意**」 — this card is covered by 「其他同意」, i.e. approved as presented: option B.

⚠️ **Record-keeping gap, named rather than hidden:** this card was moved to `needs-user-decision` at 09:26Z with no recording comment (the comment thread was empty when it was presented). It was presented anyway because scope item 4 is a genuine product call; whoever flipped it should leave a one-line note next time.

### The ruling

**Option B.** The unit of action is **the organization's claim**, not the user — the same principle #15409 landed (ruling B there: drop the unbacked claim, do not refuse the principal):

- A session whose `activeOrganizationId` points at the organization the membership just ended in loses that claim: it is cleared, or re-pointed to a membership the user still holds. A user who still holds other memberships is **not** signed out of them; they switch to an organization they still belong to.
- A user with **no remaining membership** has nothing left to be signed into; for that user the session is revoked through the existing `sys_session.revoked_at` / `revoke_reason` mechanism with a new event-driven reason naming the cause, and the card's acceptance (next request unauthenticated, Console redirects to login) applies to exactly this case. ⚠️ This is the seat's application of the approved option where the option text is silent; the maintainer can flip it in one line.
- ⛔ A (revoke every session of the user) is rejected — it logs people out of organizations they legitimately belong to. ⛔ C (do nothing) is rejected — the admin was told the person was removed.
- Scope item 3 stands verbatim: ⛔ never weaken, bypass or optimise away #15409's per-request check on the strength of this trigger; the comment beside the check says why (a trigger can be missed, an evaluation cannot).

### Execution

- **Precondition = scope item 1**: enumerate every writer that can delete or invalidate a `sys_member` row — this repo **and** cloud's `packages/organizations` — by measurement with a firing control, attached to the card before the trigger is wired. A path the census misses fails open only to a stale claim, which #15409 already neutralises per request.
- **Seat:** `domain:services`, `pm:queue`. The spent `Blocked-by: #15409` line is removed from the body (#15409 closed `completed` via PR #15794, merged 09:25Z).
- **Clause-②: `yes`** — a new `revoke_reason` value on a published system object is an accept-set widening; re-judge from the diff.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` `minor` (the new reason value) + the implementing package `patch`; the dev derives the exact set from the diff.
- **Acceptance, restated under B:** an admin removes a member through better-auth's own endpoint while that member has a live session → that session no longer resolves the removed organization (re-pointed if the user holds another membership, revoked if not). Controls: a member of a different organization unaffected; an intact member's session untouched; the #15409 pins still hold.

Labels: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:services`, `security`, `priority:p2` stay.

**The record-keeping gap named in the ruling above is mine, and it is correctly named.**

I flipped this card to `needs-user-decision` at 09:26Z inside a batch of label writes and left **no comment on this card at all** — verified: zero. My reasoning was in the session chat and in #15409's landing readback, and neither is visible to a seat opening this card. That is exactly the "结论只在 chat" half-state this loop has spent the day correcting in other people's cards, and the director seat had to reconstruct the intent to present it. ⇒ It was presented anyway and ruled, so nothing was lost this time; the discipline was.

**The note I should have left, recorded now for the thread's own history:**

> Moved to `needs-user-decision` because scope item 4 is a product call the implementer must not make for the maintainer: what happens to a user who holds **other** memberships. Revoking every session logs them out of organizations they are still legitimately in; re-pointing `activeOrganizationId` is kinder but has to say *to which*. The card is otherwise fully specified and its enforcement half (#15409) had just landed, so this was the only thing standing between it and dispatch.

**Acknowledged and unchanged**: the ruling stands as recorded — **B, act on the organization's claim, never on the user**, with the seat's application where the option text is silent (re-point when another membership remains, revoke when none does) flagged there as flippable in one line. Dispatching on that basis now.

Claim: PM loop — maintainer direct-dispatch channel (2026-08-10 standing authorization); this card is the courtesy half of the #15409 family this session has carried end to end.

## Scope item 1 — the membership-removal census, with its firing controls

Posted **before** the trigger is wired, as the ruling requires. Measured against
`objectstack` `59953d5a3` (this branch's base) and `cloud` `3856fbf7c`.

Three readings, each with its own control. Where a control is dead or over-firing the
run reports nothing — that is enforced in the detector, not promised in prose.

### Reading A — writers that NAME the table

Detector: a windowed scan (4 lines) for a write verb whose argument names the member
object — `sys_member`, `SystemObjectName.MEMBER`, `MEMBERSHIP_OBJECT`,
`AUTH_MEMBER_SCHEMA` — across `delete` / `deleteMany` / `bulkDelete` / `deleteOne` /
`remove` / `destroy` (ending the row) and `update` / `updateMany` / `bulkUpdate` /
`upsert` / `replace` (invalidating it), plus raw-SQL `DELETE FROM` / `TRUNCATE` /
`DROP TABLE` shapes and the declarative `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` shape.

**Firing control**: a synthetic file carrying one instance of every shape.

```
CONTROL shapes lit: cascade:deleteBehavior, delete:bulkDelete, delete:delete,
                    delete:deleteMany, invalidate:update, invalidate:updateMany, raw-sql:sql
CONTROL VERDICT: FIRING — all 7 shapes lit
```

Results:

| root | files | production hits |
|---|---|---|
| `objectstack/packages` | 5517 | **3** |
| `cloud/packages` | 755 | **0** |

The three, in full:

- `platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts:263` — `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`
  on `user_id`. A `sys_user` delete takes its memberships (line 255 is the same token
  inside the comment above it).
- `plugins/plugin-auth/src/adopt-membership.ts:230` — `engine.update(SystemObjectName.MEMBER, …)`,
  invitation acceptance adopting an existing row. It re-points nothing that ends a
  membership; recorded for completeness.

**Zero delete call sites that name the table.** That is a true answer to a misleading
question, and Reading B exists because of it.

### Reading B — the GENERIC doors (the ones that never spell `sys_member`)

better-auth's ObjectQL adapter deletes through a **variable** object name —
`dataEngine.delete(objectName, …)`, `objectql-adapter.ts:1023/1039/1056/1180/1188` — so
the dominant removal path is invisible to Reading A by construction. This reading
enumerates deletes whose object argument is a runtime expression, then classifies each by
which abstraction the receiver holds: the ObjectQL **engine** (every registered hook
fires) or a raw **driver** (hooks do not).

**Firing control**: four positive shapes plus two negatives that must NOT be reported (a
literal-named delete, and a `Map.delete` on a cache). The first run of this detector
**failed its own control by over-firing** on `membershipCache.delete(cacheKey)`; the
leaf-name test was tightened and re-run.

```
CONTROL positives lit: bulkDelete/driver-or-raw, delete/engine,
                       deleteMany/driver-or-raw, deleteMany/engine  (n=4)
CONTROL negatives reported (must be 0): 0
CONTROL VERDICT: FIRING and not over-firing
```

The doors that can carry a membership row:

| # | site | abstraction | reaches an engine hook? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `plugin-auth/objectql-adapter.ts:1023,1039,1056,1180,1188` — every better-auth delete, `/organization/remove-member` included | engine | yes |
| 2 | `plugin-auth/objectql-adapter.ts:707` — the attributed-system engine wrapper | engine | yes |
| 3 | cloud `service-cloud/routes/package-install.ts:1210` — `envDriver.delete(objectName, id)`, the package-uninstall sample-data purge, object name taken from the package's own manifest datasets and **ungated** | raw driver | **NO** |
| 4 | cloud `service-cloud/control-plane-proxy-driver.ts:124,136` | raw driver | NO (control-plane tables only) |

Doors examined and **excluded**, with the reason: `plugin-sharing/record-orphan-cleanup.ts`
and `plugin-security/auto-org-admin-grant.ts` are generic over a table name their callers
pass as a literal (share / grant tables); cloud's
`service-tenant/environment-provisioning.ts:1578,1584` and
`service-cloud/routes/environment-crud.ts:262` cascade over a **closed literal list** of
four environment tables that does not contain `sys_member`.

### Reading C — the runtime probe (what actually reaches the seam)

A probe registered on `sys_member` for `beforeDelete` / `afterDelete` / `beforeUpdate` /
`afterUpdate`, on a real booted stack (`bootStack(showcaseStack)`, real better-auth, real
HTTP), then each enumerated path driven for real. Path 0 is the firing control: if a
direct engine delete does not light the probe, nothing else in the table is a reading.

```
PATH 0  engine.delete (direct)                 -> beforeDelete,afterDelete
PATH 1  better-auth /organization/remove-member -> HTTP 200; row gone=true; beforeDelete,afterDelete
PATH 2  engine.delete multi:true               -> beforeDelete,afterDelete
PATH 3  cascade via sys_user delete            -> row gone=true; beforeDelete,afterDelete
PATH 4  driver.delete (raw, hooks bypassed)    -> row gone=true; NOTHING
PATH 5  engine.update re-point organization_id -> beforeUpdate,afterUpdate
```

`Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 6 passed (6)`. Path 3 needed its own correction: the
first run reported `row gone=false; NOTHING; refused: This User is still referenced by 1
Session record(s)` — `sys_session.user_id` and `sys_account.user_id` are required lookups
that restrict, so the user delete never happened and the cascade was never measured. With
those cleared first, the cascade runs and the membership row's own hooks fire, one row
deeper, exactly as `sys-member.object.ts` documents.

### cloud's `packages/organizations` — measured, and it is genuinely empty

`packages/organizations/src` contains **zero** references to `sys_member` /
`SystemObjectName.MEMBER`, and its only writes at all are two `ql.update` calls on
`owner_id` (`claim-orphan-org-rows.ts:106`, `claim-org-seed-ownership.ts:93`). The same
grep fires 34 times elsewhere in the same repo and 3 times in `objectstack`, so this zero
is a reading and not a dead detector. Membership creation in cloud lives in
`service-cloud/personal-org-hook.ts` and `objectos-runtime/environment-org-seed.ts` — both
**create only**. Removal in cloud is delegated to `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, i.e. to
Reading B row 1.

### What the census decides

The seam is an **engine hook on `sys_member`**, not a hook on better-auth's
`/organization/remove-member` endpoint. Rows 1, 2 and paths 0/1/2/3/5 all reach it; an
endpoint hook would reach exactly one of them. This is also the precedent already in the
file: `last-admin-guard.ts` enforces its invariant with `beforeUpdate` / `beforeDelete` on
`sys_member` for the same stated reason — an HTTP guard protects only the endpoint it is
attached to.

### The one measured gap, stated plainly

**A raw driver delete bypasses the trigger completely** (path 4, `NOTHING`), and there is
a real production caller of that shape: cloud's package-uninstall sample-data purge takes
its object name from the installed package's manifest and calls `envDriver.delete` with
no allow-list, so a package declaring a dataset over `sys_member` removes membership rows
with no hook, no audit row and no revocation. That is the card's own "a seed replay, a
bulk operation, a control-plane operation" made concrete.

It is also exactly why this card is the courtesy and not the wall: the same removal leaves
a stale claim that per-request enforcement already neutralises. Filed as **cloud#2003**
rather than fixed here (this card must not grow a cloud arm), and the trigger's own
documentation names this path as the known-open one.

## Gates — 108 derived, 99 green, 9 NOT MEASURED

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived its own change
set (14 paths, three-dot against merge base `59953d5a3`) at `24536a537`. It was re-derived
after the docs edits, which pulled in **21 gates the first derivation did not name**.

**Four were genuinely red and are fixed**: `check:doc-authoring` (six tracker ids in runtime
log strings — moved to comments); `check:objectql-double-limit` and `check:where-matcher`
(the new test double ignored `limit` and read a combinator as a field name — it now applies
the bound by presence after the filter, refuses what it does not implement, and its matcher
was moved to module scope so both gates can lift and judge it);
`check:system-context-census` and `check:tenant-audit-census` (an anchor rotted on a line
shift; the write-call-site census moved 219 to 221, regenerated with its 23 prose figures).

**The nine non-zero results are all NOT MEASURED, with reasons:**

| gate | exit | why it is not a verdict |
|---|---|---|

| `check:single-claim-paths` | 2 | NOT WIRED — needs `PR_NUMBER`; CI supplies it |
| `check:test-completeness` | 3 | exited before parsing a summary line; its own text says it is not a finding |
| `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` | 3 | PREREQUISITE NOT MET — 7 packages have no `dist/` |
| `check:published-readme-exports` | 3 | PREREQUISITE NOT MET — reads built type surface |
| `check:skill-examples` | 1 | `client-react/dist` holds no `.d.ts`; the gate refuses rather than green |
| `check:react-declaration-parity` | 1 | needs an objectui manifest and a browser dump |
| `pr-labels.mjs` | 1 | usage error — the runner invoked it with no mode flag |
| `check:merge-driver` | 1 | **pre-existing and environmental**: two self-test cases about "a gate whose RUNNER is not installed" fail on this host, and `git diff 59953d5a3 -- scripts/ .gitattributes` is empty, so the verdict cannot be a function of this diff |

`check:closing-keyword-parity` was also run with the real PR body and passed, so the one
closing keyword in it (`Fixes #15784`) is the only one, by measurement.

**Declared narrowing — verification ran UNLOCKED.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` could not
take the shared verify lock on this host: no usable `flock` (it is util-linux; a stock macOS
does not ship it). Every command was run directly, without the lock — a declared narrowing,
not a silent one. No serialization guarantee held for these runs.

## For the PM's records

The dispatch cited the maintainer's ruling as comment **5551086286**. That id 404s on the
issue-comment, PR-review-comment and cloud endpoints and does not appear in this repo's
comment stream (it would sit between `5551085989` at 10:10:05Z and `5551088281` at
10:10:36Z). The ruling actually recorded on this card is **5551140528**, and its content
matches what the dispatch restated word for word — so nothing was lost, and the work was
done against the real ruling.

**Correction to my dispatch, and the census finding that should outlive this card.**

**My error**: the dispatch cited the ruling as comment `5551086286`. That id **404s** — I mistyped it. The real ruling is **5551140528** on this card, by the director seat, and its content is what the dispatch restated, so nothing was lost. ⭐ The dev checked the citation instead of working around it and reported the mismatch — that is the right reflex, and it is worth saying so: a dispatch that cites a comment nobody can open is a dispatch whose provenance cannot be audited.

## ⭐ The census found two things that change how this fix should be read

**1. The dominant removal path never names `sys_member`.** better-auth's adapter deletes through a **variable** object name, so a detector that scans for the literal `sys_member` honestly reports **zero** deletes on the path that does most of the removing. A census run that way would have come back clean and been wrong. The probe measured through a real booted stack with hooks registered and a firing control instead — six paths driven, five fire.

**2. A raw driver delete bypasses every engine hook, and there is a real production caller.** PATH 4 in the probe: the row is gone and **nothing** fires. That is not hypothetical — it is filed as **cloud#2003**: package uninstall's sample-data purge deletes any object the manifest names through the raw environment driver with no allow-list, identity tables included. Both `last-admin-guard`'s `beforeDelete` **and** this card's trigger fail open on it.

⇒ **This is precisely why the ruling put the enforcement on #15409 and not here.** A trigger covers the paths that go through hooks; PATH 4 does not. The per-request check does not care which path deleted the row. ⛔ The scope item 3 prohibition — never weaken #15409's check on the strength of this trigger — is now backed by a measured hole, not a principle. Verified on the PR: `resolve-authz-context.ts` is **not in the diff**.

## Two divergences, both declared rather than taken quietly

1. **There is no `packages/spec` carrier for `revoke_reason`** — the column is a free `Field.text` with no Zod enum, so the accept-set widening lands on `@objectstack/platform-objects`, whose published field description *is* the vocabulary. Changeset accordingly: `platform-objects` **minor** + `plugin-auth` **minor** (three new public exports, so not the `patch` the dispatch assumed). The dispatch's 「`@objectstack/spec` minor」 was wrong about the carrier; the dev measured the tree and said so.
2. The ruling's second bullet — revoke when no membership remains — was applied as the director seat wrote it, including the clearing case when the remaining membership carries no organization id.

Reviewing for landing now.

## The lesson worth keeping, since it cost a CI round

`dispatch-gates` prints gate bullets at **two indent levels** — path-derived families at two
spaces, and *Convention-triggered* / *Always runs* families at four. Scraping its
human-readable output with a two-space anchor drops the deeper section **silently and with
exit 0**, which is the exact failure shape the repo's own gate-reading discipline warns
about: a well-formed green answer to a question nobody asked.

The tool already solves this — `--commands` emits the pasteable list, with the flags CI
actually uses (`--self-test`, `--base origin/main`, `--advisory`), and its output explicitly
says a bare run of one of those scripts "is an invocation CI never makes". Last round's
bare-form runs were therefore the wrong invocation for roughly two dozen gates, even where
they happened to agree. **Use `--commands`; do not scrape the prose.**

## The census is the part worth keeping

Run first and posted before anything was wired, with its own firing controls, over `objectstack@59953d5a3` and `cloud@3856fbf7c`. Two findings shaped the work:

1. ⭐ **The dominant removal path never names `sys_member`.** better-auth's adapter deletes through a **variable** object name, so a detector scanning for the literal name honestly reports **zero** deletes on the path that does most of the removing. A census run that way comes back clean and is wrong. The probe drove six paths through a real booted stack with hooks registered; five fire.
2. ⭐ **PATH 4 — a raw driver delete — bypasses every engine hook, and there is a real production caller.** Filed as **cloud#2003**: package uninstall's sample-data purge deletes any object the manifest names through the raw environment driver with no allow-list, identity tables included. `last-admin-guard`'s `beforeDelete` **and** this card's trigger both fail open on it.

⇒ **This is why the ruling put the enforcement on #15409 and the courtesy here.** A trigger covers the paths that go through hooks; PATH 4 does not. The per-request check does not care which path deleted the row. Scope item 3's prohibition — never weaken that check on the strength of this trigger — is now backed by a **measured** hole rather than a principle.
